title: 你在臺灣學多久的中文？ How Long Will You Be Studying Chinese in Taiwan?

paras.text: Topic: 學習、工作 Study, Work
• Learning to discuss study plans and future plans.
• Learning to talk about sequences of events.
• Learning to describe past actions and experience.
Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue I. The book’s own Dialogue I is on book p. 246 (PDF p. 273); its recording is track 12-01.

lines.zh: 安同，你計畫在臺灣念多久的書？
lines.py: Āntóng, nǐ jìhuà zài Táiwān niàn duō jiǔ de shū?

lines.zh: 三年。
lines.py: Sān nián.

lines.zh: 為什麼要這麼久的時間？
lines.py: Wèishénme yào zhème jiǔ de shíjiān?

lines.zh: 我先在語言中心念半年，再念兩年半的大學，所以需要三年。
lines.py: Wǒ xiān zài yǔyán zhōngxīn niàn bàn nián, zài niàn liǎng nián bàn de dàxué, suǒyǐ xūyào sān nián.

lines.zh: 這得花不少錢！
lines.py: Zhè děi huā bù shǎo qián!

lines.zh: 對，不過我有獎學金。要是成績不好，就沒獎學金了。你呢？
lines.py: Duì, búguò wǒ yǒu jiǎngxuéjīn. Yàoshì chéngjī bù hǎo, jiù méi jiǎngxuéjīn le. Nǐ ne?

lines.zh: 我的學費是爸媽替我付的。
lines.py: Wǒ de xuéfèi shì bàmā tì wǒ fù de.

lines.zh: 妳打算學多久呢？
lines.py: Nǐ dǎsuàn xué duō jiǔ ne?

lines.zh: 大概一年，是我自己決定的。
lines.py: Dàgài yì nián, shì wǒ zìjǐ juédìng de.

lines.zh: 希望我以後也可以像妳一樣，說一口好聽的中文。
lines.py: Xīwàng wǒ yǐhòu yě kěyǐ xiàng nǐ yíyàng, shuō yì kǒu hǎotīng de Zhōngwén.

lines.zh: 我又要上課，又要打工，真的很累。
lines.py: Wǒ yòu yào shàngkè, yòu yào dǎgōng, zhēnde hěn lèi.

lines.zh: 我們一起加油吧！
lines.py: Wǒmen yìqǐ jiāyóu ba!

translation.en: Antong, how long do you plan to study in Taiwan?
Three years.
Why such a long time?
I’m going to study for half a year at the language center first, then two and a half years at university, so I need three years.
That’s going to cost a lot of money!
True, but I have a scholarship. If my grades are poor, I’ll lose it. And you?
My tuition is paid by my parents for me.
How long do you plan to study?
About a year — that’s my own decision.
I hope I can speak Chinese as nicely as you do someday.
I have to both go to class and work part-time. It’s really exhausting.
Let’s keep up the good work together!

items.en: measure word for a mouthful, a language spoken

paras.text: Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue II. The book’s own Dialogue II is on book p. 249 (PDF p. 276); its recording is track 12-03.

lines.zh: 田中，你是什麼時候來臺灣工作的？
lines.py: Tiánzhōng, nǐ shì shénme shíhòu lái Táiwān gōngzuò de?

lines.zh: 去年，我已經在臺灣工作一年半了。
lines.py: Qùnián, wǒ yǐjīng zài Táiwān gōngzuò yì nián bàn le.

lines.zh: 為什麼你們公司要替你付學費？
lines.py: Wèishénme nǐmen gōngsī yào tì nǐ fù xuéfèi?

lines.zh: 因為我們公司跟很多臺灣人做生意，老闆希望大家都會說中文。
lines.py: Yīnwèi wǒmen gōngsī gēn hěn duō Táiwān rén zuò shēngyì, lǎobǎn xīwàng dàjiā dōu huì shuō Zhōngwén.

lines.zh: 我覺得你們公司真好。
lines.py: Wǒ juéde nǐmen gōngsī zhēn hǎo.

lines.zh: 對了，妳回國以後，打算做什麼？
lines.py: Duìle, nǐ huíguó yǐhòu, dǎsuàn zuò shénme?

lines.zh: 我回國以後，也想找個有機會說中文的工作。
lines.py: Wǒ huíguó yǐhòu, yě xiǎng zhǎo ge yǒu jīhuì shuō Zhōngwén de gōngzuò.

lines.zh: 不錯，這樣的工作在妳們國家好找嗎？
lines.py: Búcuò, zhèyàng de gōngzuò zài nǐmen guójiā hǎo zhǎo ma?

lines.zh: 不知道好不好找，我試試看。
lines.py: Bù zhīdào hǎo bù hǎo zhǎo, wǒ shìshìkàn.

lines.zh: 要是難找呢？
lines.py: Yàoshì nán zhǎo ne?

lines.zh: 那麼我再來臺灣學中文。
lines.py: Nàme wǒ zài lái Táiwān xué Zhōngwén.

lines.zh: 太好了！那我們就可以再見面了。
lines.py: Tài hǎo le! Nà wǒmen jiù kěyǐ zài jiànmiàn le.

translation.en: Tanaka, when did you come to Taiwan to work?
Last year. I’ve already been working in Taiwan for a year and a half.
Why does your company pay your tuition for you?
Because our company does business with a lot of Taiwanese people, and my boss wants everyone to be able to speak Chinese.
I think your company is really good.
By the way, what do you plan to do after you go back to your country?
After I go back, I’d also like to find a job that gives me a chance to speak Chinese.
Not bad — is that kind of job easy to find in your country?
I don’t know if it’s easy to find, but I’ll give it a try.
And if it’s hard to find?
Then I’ll come back to Taiwan to study Chinese.
Great! Then we can see each other again.

items.en: to give it a try, to try and see what happens

blocks.en: I. 先 xiān…，再 zài… first…, and then…

paras.text: Use: This pattern presents the temporal sequence of two consecutive events — first one event happens, then the other. It can describe the order of two events in either the past or the future.

items.zh: 我計畫先在語言中心學中文，再念大學。
items.py: Wǒ jìhuà xiān zài yǔyán zhōngxīn xué Zhōngwén, zài niàn dàxué.
items.en: I plan to study Chinese at the language center first, and then go to university.

items.zh: 她想先找工作，再決定要不要念書。
items.py: Tā xiǎng xiān zhǎo gōngzuò, zài juédìng yào bú yào niànshū.
items.en: She wants to look for a job first, and then decide whether to study.

items.zh: 我昨天先寫功課，再看電視。
items.py: Wǒ zuótiān xiān xiě gōngkè, zài kàn diànshì.
items.en: Yesterday I did my homework first, and then watched TV.

items.zh: 我明天先去圖書館看書，再去找工作。
items.py: Wǒ míngtiān xiān qù túshūguǎn kànshū, zài qù zhǎo gōngzuò.
items.en: Tomorrow I’ll go to the library to read first, and then go job-hunting.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete each sentence with 先…再….

items.prompt: 我們明天要先去銀行，再＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: II. To Focus with 是 shì…的 de

paras.text: Use: This pattern highlights one element in a sentence about a past event and marks it as the focus — the main message of the sentence. The focus marker 是 goes directly before the focused element, and 的 goes at the end of the sentence (Subject + 是 + Focus + Activity + 的). The object is often moved to the very front of the sentence.

The focused element can be the subject, the time, the place, the manner, and occasionally the verb — but never the object. 是 can be omitted; the pattern can also ask a wh-question (who, when, how, where) about a past event, but it does not work when “what” is the object. 不 always goes before 是.

items.zh: 他是去年來臺灣工作的。
items.py: Tā shì qùnián lái Táiwān gōngzuò de.
items.en: It was last year that he came to Taiwan to work. (time)

items.py: Xuéfèi shì bàmā tì wǒ fù de.
items.en: It is my parents who pay my tuition for me. (object fronted)

items.py: Shì wǒ dǎ diànhuà gěi lǎobǎn de.
items.en: It was I who called the boss. (subject)

items.zh: 他是坐高鐵來臺北上班的。
items.py: Tā shì zuò gāotiě lái Táiběi shàngbān de.
items.en: It was by High Speed Rail that he came to Taipei for work. (manner)

items.zh: 她不是去年找到工作的。
items.py: Tā búshì qùnián zhǎo dào gōngzuò de.
items.en: It was not last year that she found the job.

items.py: Búshì wǒ juédìng yào dǎgōng de.
items.en: It wasn’t I who decided to work part-time.

items.zh: 你是什麼時候開始打工的？
items.py: Nǐ shì shénme shíhòu kāishǐ dǎgōng de?
items.en: When did you start working part-time?

items.zh: 你的獎學金是怎麼申請的？
items.py: Nǐ de jiǎngxuéjīn shì zěnme shēnqǐng de?
items.en: How did you apply for your scholarship?

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Answer each question using 是…的, focusing on the element asked about.

items.prompt: 他是什麼時候來臺灣的？（去年九月）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
這筆獎學金是誰申請的？（我自己）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
你是怎麼找到這個工作的？（朋友介紹）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

paras.text: Use: 以後 is basically a noun with two functions here. Used alone, like a time word, it means “some time in the future”: 我以後想當老師 (In the future, I’d like to become a teacher). Used together with an event — Event + 以後, Result — it connects two events sequentially, meaning “after Event, Result”.

items.zh: 我以後想找一個常常要說中文的工作。
items.py: Wǒ yǐhòu xiǎng zhǎo yí ge chángcháng yào shuō Zhōngwén de gōngzuò.
items.en: In the future, I’d like to find a job where I often need to speak Chinese. (alone)

items.zh: 畢業以後，我要回國找工作。
items.py: Bìyè yǐhòu, wǒ yào huíguó zhǎo gōngzuò.
items.en: After graduating, I’m going to go back to my country to find a job.

items.zh: 來臺灣以後，我每天都說中文。
items.py: Lái Táiwān yǐhòu, wǒ měi tiān dōu shuō Zhōngwén.
items.en: Since coming to Taiwan, I speak Chinese every day.

items.zh: 下課以後，我常在圖書館打工。
items.py: Xiàkè yǐhòu, wǒ cháng zài túshūguǎn dǎgōng.
items.en: After class, I often work part-time at the library.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete each sentence using 以後.

items.prompt: 大學畢業＿＿＿＿＿＿，我想先工作，再念書。
來臺灣＿＿＿＿＿＿，你的中文進步了嗎？

blocks.en: IV. Special Meanings of 好 hǎo / 難 nán + Verbs

paras.text: Use: When 好 or 難 combine with perception verbs (吃, 喝, 看, 聽…), they form single words meaning “nice/not nice to [do]” — 好吃/難吃, 好喝/難喝, 好看/難看, 好聽/難聽. When they combine with action verbs, 好 means “easy to” and 難 means “difficult/hard to” — 好學/難學, 好找/難找, 好做/難做, 好寫/難寫.
Degree adverbs such as 很 can modify both structures.

items.zh: 這份工作的薪水不錯，可是不好找。
items.py: Zhè fèn gōngzuò de xīnshuǐ búcuò, kěshì bù hǎo zhǎo.
items.en: This job pays well, but it’s hard to find.

items.zh: 老師說的中文故事很好聽。
items.py: Lǎoshī shuō de Zhōngwén gùshì hěn hǎotīng.
items.en: The Chinese story the teacher told was lovely to listen to.

items.zh: 有人覺得這個獎學金的申請表很難寫。
items.py: Yǒu rén juéde zhè ge jiǎngxuéjīn de shēnqǐngbiǎo hěn nán xiě.
items.en: Some people find this scholarship application form hard to fill out.

items.py: Wǒ māma zuò de cài hěn hǎochī.
items.en: The food my mom makes is delicious.

items.zh: 便宜的學校餐廳，菜不難吃。
items.py: Piányí de xuéxiào cāntīng, cài bù nánchī.
items.en: The food at the cheap school cafeteria isn’t bad.

items.zh: 說中文的工作在我的國家不好找。
items.py: Shuō Zhōngwén de gōngzuò zài wǒ de guójiā bù hǎo zhǎo.
items.en: Jobs where you speak Chinese aren’t easy to find in my country.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Comment on each item using a 好/難 + verb combination.

items.prompt: 這個老闆教的書法…（好看）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
學校附近便宜的套房…（難找）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: I. What 小美 Has Planned

paras.text: Goal: Learning to talk about sequences of events.
Task: Read 小美 Xiaomei’s schedule for a Friday and decide whether each statement below is true (T) or false (F).
8:00 am 跟爸爸到學校付學費；9:00–12:00 上中文課；12:00 到老師家吃中飯；2:00–3:00 學書法；3:10–4:00 聽古典音樂；5:00 跟同學去看電影；8:00 pm 買晚飯。
小美她那天……1. （ ）先去學校，再去吃飯。 2. （ ）先吃中飯，再上中文課。 3. （ ）先買晚飯，再去看電影。
4. （ ）先上中文課，再學書法。 5. （ ）先去老師家，再去看電影。

blocks.en: II. A Day in 大朋 Dapeng’s Life

paras.text: Goal: Learning to discuss things that your friends have done.
Task 1: Pair up with a classmate. Take turns asking and answering questions about what 大朋 did yesterday, using 是…的 with the cue given for each picture: 1. 在哪裡／買 2. 怎麼來（去） 3. 什麼時候 4. 跟（誰） 5. 誰.
e.g. 大朋的咖啡是在那家便利商店買的。
Task 2: Bring a few photos to class and use 是…的 to describe them, e.g. 這張照片是在…照的／是去年三月照的／是跟朋友一起照的／…是怎麼去的／是…幫我們照的。

blocks.en: III. What Are Your Study Plans?

paras.text: Goal: Learning to describe study plans and future plans.
Task: Tell the class about your own plans: how long you’ve been in Taiwan, how long you plan to stay, your future study plans (in Taiwan or back in your country), and your future career plans.
Goal: Learning to describe your experience.
Task: If you have any work experience, share it with the class — what the job was, how you found it, and how long you did it. Other students should ask follow-up questions once you’re done.
Being polite at all times is considered important in Chinese culture, and the workplace is no exception — how people are addressed depends on several factors.

The most common way to address someone is by their job title: a manager might be called 王經理 Wáng Jīnglǐ (“Manager Wang”), or a professor 李教授 Lǐ Jiàoshòu (“Professor Li”). People may also be addressed by the highest academic title they hold — 陳博士 Chén Bóshì (“Dr. Chen”), or more fully 文學博士陳月文 Wénxué Bóshì Chén Yuèwén (“Dr. of Literature Chen Yuewen”). Another method is by profession, such as 張老師 Zhāng Lǎoshī (“Teacher Zhang”) or 王議員 Wáng Yìyuán (“MP Wang”, a member of parliament). When someone’s title or profession is unknown, 小姐 (Miss), 女士 (Madam), or 先生 (Mister) are also polite.

blocks.en: Privacy Means Something Different for Taiwanese

paras.text: Taiwanese people sometimes ask friends from abroad questions like “Where do you work?”, “How much do you make?”, “Are you married?”, “How many children do you have?”, and “Are they boys or girls?” While many foreigners consider these kinds of questions intrusive, in Taiwanese culture they’re generally seen as a sign of interest and a way of breaking the ice.

items: I can discuss study plans and future plans.
I can talk about sequences of events.
I can describe past actions and experience.
